label: Dentist visit

what_happens.title: What happens at the dentist
goals: A dentist is a doctor who keeps teeth strong and clean
The visit follows the same steps every time: door, waiting room, big chair, counting teeth, a sticker
Nothing is a surprise: the dentist shows and tells before doing
what_happens.parentSkill: Name the steps in order and ask your child to say what comes next.

who_is_there.title: Who is at the dentist
goals: The front desk helper, the dental assistant and the dentist each have one job
They wear masks and gloves to keep everyone clean, and smile behind the mask
The grown-up stays close the whole time
who_is_there.parentSkill: Talk about the helpers by their job, so new faces feel like part of the plan.

what_i_do.title: What I do in the big chair
goals: The child's jobs: sit back, open wide, keep hands on the tummy
Raising a hand means 'I need a break', and the dentist stops
The child can count teeth with the dentist
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise 'open wide' and the stop signal with a mirror and a toothbrush.

if_scared.title: If I feel scared
goals: Feeling scared is okay and many children feel it
Some things may tickle, press or pinch a little, and that feeling ends
Calm-down tools: slow breaths, holding a hand or a foot, sunglasses for the bright light
if_scared.parentSkill: Name the feeling without fixing it: 'You feel worried. I'm right here.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the dentist
goals: Play dentist at home with a toothbrush and a toy
Go through every step once more, ending with the sticker
Celebrate the child's bravery and the plan for afterwards
rehearsal.parentSkill: Let your child be the dentist first, then switch roles.

steps: Walk in through the clinic door and say hello at the front desk
Wait in the waiting room until the child's name is called
Sit in the big chair that moves up and leans back
Put on sunglasses for the bright light above
Open wide while the dentist counts and checks each tooth with a tiny mirror
Teeth are cleaned with a buzzy brush and rinsed with water
Pick a sticker and go home
sensory: a bright lamp over the chair
a buzzing sound from the little brush
a minty or fruity taste of toothpaste
cool water and a slurpy straw that sucks it up
a chair that hums as it moves
gloves and masks on the helpers
a little straw that slurps the water away
dentist toothpaste that tastes fruity and feels gritty
honestyNotes: May feel a little pinch, press or tickle. Never promise 'no pain'. Say the feeling is short and the dentist stops when the child raises a hand.

questionButtons.text: Why is the light so bright?
fallbackAnswer: The bright light helps the dentist see inside your mouth.
You can wear sunglasses, and you can close your eyes too.
A dentist is a doctor whose job is keeping teeth healthy.
The dentist will say hello and tell you each step before doing it.
When your teeth are counted and clean, the chair goes back down.
Then you pick a sticker, and you go home with [[GROWNUP]].
Sometimes the dentist asks you to rinse and spit into a little sink.

questionButtons.text: What does the toothpaste taste like?
fallbackAnswer: Dentist toothpaste can taste like fruit or mint, and it feels a bit gritty.
If you do not like it, you can say so, and they will rinse it away.

questionButtons.text: What is the picture of my teeth?
fallbackAnswer: Sometimes the dentist takes a picture of your teeth with a special camera.
You bite on something small and keep still for a moment, and then it is done.

techniques.label: Holding a hand or a foot
techniques.how: Sit or stand where your child can reach you and hold a hand or a foot during the check.

techniques.label: Counting teeth together
techniques.how: Ask the dentist to count teeth out loud and count along in your head or with your fingers.

techniques.label: Counting to ten
techniques.how: Count slowly to ten together during each part of the check; many parts are done before ten.

techniques.label: Wearing sunglasses
techniques.how: Bring your child's own sunglasses or ask for a pair to soften the bright lamp.

techniques.label: Choosing a sticker after
techniques.how: Talk about the sticker or a small treat at the end, so there is something to look forward to.

techniques.label: The hand-up stop signal
techniques.how: Agree with the dentist that a raised hand means 'please wait', and practise it at home.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out through the mouth like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Bringing a comfort toy
techniques.how: Let your child bring a favourite toy to hold in the waiting room and in the chair.

techniques.label: Tell, show, do
techniques.how: Ask the dentist to tell what each tool does, show it on a finger, then use it.

techniques.label: Practising with a mirror
techniques.how: Practise 'open wide' and counting teeth in front of a mirror at home.

Going to the dentist is something many children do.
A check-up has a clear order, and knowing it makes the visit feel shorter.
[[CHILD]] checks in at the front desk, waits a little, and then goes to a room with a chair that tilts back.

A cleaning comes next, and the visit ends with a plan for keeping teeth strong.

Several people work together at a dental office, and each has a real job.
The receptionist keeps track of visits.

The assistant passes tools and runs the little suction straw that pulls water out of the mouth.
